rows.note: Use 建議 as the everyday all-purpose verb when explicitly recommending a course of action or option.

example.english: I suggest you take the MTR there.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gin3 ji5 nei5 daap3 dei6 tit3 heoi3

rows.note: Use 提議 when “suggest” means propose, especially when putting forward a concrete option for consideration rather than mainly recommending it.

example.english: I suggest holding the meeting next week.
example.jyutping: ngo5 tai4 ji5 haa6 sing1 kei4 hoi1 wui2

rows.note: Use 暗示 when implying something without stating it openly.

example.english: That way of putting it can suggest that he does not want to help.
example.traditional: 佢咁樣講，暗示緊佢唔想幫手。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gam2 joeng2 gong2 am3 si6 gan2 keoi5 m4 soeng2 bong1 sau2

rows.note: Use 令人諗到 when something causes people to think of or infer an idea, rather than when a person deliberately hints at it.

example.english: This painting can suggest a rainy day.
example.traditional: 呢幅畫令人諗到一個落雨天。
example.jyutping: ni1 fuk1 waa2 ling6 jan4 nam2 dou3 jat1 go3 lok6 jyu5 tin1
